payload.methods: Applies the registered test to every successful project in Web Robots' crawl of 22 April 2014, the earliest listed on its dataset page. Outcome: failed if success_p25_over > 0.06 or success_median_over > 0.20 (nearest rank; over-funding = pledged/goal - 1), else confirmed. Deviation: the test asks for a complete crawl, which cannot be proved; a lower-bound check fixed in advance stands in (at least 48,526 projects launched by July 2012, Mollick's cleaned N), else inconclusive. Early crawls' selection is undocumented, so the direction of any bias is unknown. Filters as Chrysalis-2's 2026 receipt: first record per id in file order, state failed or successful, goal > 0, pledged >= 0. Launches to July 2012 are reported unjudged; judged figures include launches to April 2014. Prior knowledge: this file fed Instar-1's earlier pooled study, whose by-year results and per-crawl project counts were seen, so the early pattern was partly seen and the coverage check will very likely pass; none of the test's statistics was computed on this file alone. Pre-registered forecast, unchanged: P(confirmed)=0.75, P(failed)=0.2, P(inconclusive)=0.05. With Chrysalis-2's receipt, a confirmation would show only that the outcome differs between the two crawls. A first commitment (57df117905af) stopped before computing anything, having read a hidden archive file (__MACOSX) as data; it is filed as inconclusive and explained in research/receipts/mollick-2014-crawl/FIRST-ATTEMPT.md. The only change to run.py is that it reads only .json files, skipping folders and hidden entries (commit a9b0f7223a52). A smoke test then ran this bundle on the input; its code (smoke in src/v2.ts, same commit) discards printed output, checks only that all 20 output names exist, and deletes the file unread. It completed without error. Code by Claude under the operator's direction; the operator works with Dr Daniel Hulme, who founded Ecdysis and operates Chrysalis-2.
